Setting Up a New Work Tablet: A First Day Checklist

19 October 2026 Tuga Hardware

A new work tablet takes about an hour to set up properly, and that hour decides whether it earns its keep from the first job or spends a fortnight half configured in the van. The order matters more than the brand of app. Charge it, get it online, run the updates, lock it, sign in, sort storage, install and test the apps you depend on, turn on backup, then fit the protection. This checklist walks through that order and says where a Tuga device does something slightly different from a consumer tablet.

Before You Start

Set aside a quiet hour with Wi-Fi, the box, the SIM you plan to use and the login details for your main apps and cloud storage. Updates and app installs take longer on a mobile connection, so do this at home or in the office rather than on site. If you are replacing an older device, keep it switched on and signed in until the new one is working. Most of what is on it comes across through your accounts rather than a cable.

1. Fit the Battery and Charge

Some rugged devices arrive with the battery packed separately, because a removable battery is part of what makes them serviceable. The Tuga A6, Tuga A8 and Tuga WH6 come with a removable battery in the box, so the first job is fitting it. The Tuga A10 and Tuga W8 have a built-in battery and are ready to switch on.

Plug it in with the supplied UK adapter and USB-C cable and leave it charging while you work through the rest of the list. You do not need to wait for a full charge before setting up, but a first update can take a while and many devices will not install one on a low battery.

2. Get It Online and Fit the SIM

Join your Wi-Fi first, then fit the SIM. The SIM tray on a sealed device sits behind a cover that is part of the water seal, so close it properly afterwards and check the gasket has not caught on the edge. A seal that is not seated is the most common way a sealed device lets water in, and it is entirely avoidable.

One thing to know on the A6: the tray takes two Nano-SIMs, or one Nano-SIM and a microSD card. If you want the second SIM and the card, you cannot have both. Decide now rather than discovering it on a site with no signal. The A8 and A10 list dual SIM alongside a separate microSD slot. On the W10, 4G is an optional fitting rather than standard, so check what you ordered before looking for the tray.

With a SIM in, open a web page over mobile data with Wi-Fi switched off to prove the connection works. It is a thirty second test that saves a morning of wondering why photos are not uploading. Our guide to 4G, 5G or Wi-Fi only covers whether you need a SIM at all.

3. Run Every Update

Before you sign in to anything, let the device update. On Android that is Settings, then System, then System update, and it may run more than once. On Windows 11 it is Settings, then Windows Update, and it will almost certainly want a restart. Do this now because a device that updates itself on site, with a restart in the middle of a job sheet, is a device that gets left in the van. Set the update schedule to overnight or out of hours while you are in that screen.

4. Set the Screen Lock

Set a PIN before you sign in to any account that holds customer details. A tablet that lives in a van and gets handed around a site is easy to misplace, and a lock screen is the difference between losing a device and losing your customer list with it. Make the PIN six digits rather than four if the device offers it, and set the screen to lock after a short delay rather than never.

The W8 has a fingerprint sensor, which makes unlocking with gloves off quick enough that you will not be tempted to switch the lock off. The W10 lists a fingerprint reader as an optional fitting, so it depends on how yours was specified. On the Android models, use a PIN or pattern. Current Android devices encrypt their storage, and Windows 11 has device encryption in Settings, so check it is on; either way the lock is what protects the data. Our guide to protecting customer data on a work tablet goes through this in more detail, including remote wipe.

5. Sign In to the Right Account

Sign in with a work account, not a personal one. On Android that means a Google account; on Windows 11 a Microsoft account or your company's Microsoft 365 login. The account is what carries your apps, contacts, photos and backup, and it is what you use to find or wipe the device if it goes missing. If the tablet belongs to the business, use an account the business controls, so that if the person using it leaves, the device does not leave with them. A business email address on your own domain is a reasonable starting point if you do not have one.

This is also the moment to turn on the find-my-device feature, which is in the same settings area as the account on both systems. It costs nothing and you will only ever want it once.

6. Decide Where Files Live

Photos and PDF drawings fill a device faster than anything else, so decide on day one where they go. The A6 has 64GB on board and takes a microSD card up to 256GB; every other model in our range has 128GB. The A10 takes a card up to 2TB and the WH6 up to 512GB. The A8 and W10 list a card slot without a published limit, and the W8 has no card slot at all, so on the W8 the 128GB and cloud storage are what you have.

A card is cheap extra room for photos, but it is not a backup, because it goes missing with the device. If the camera app can save to the card, set that if you want the space, and set cloud storage to sync the camera folder so the photos exist somewhere else within minutes. On Android, a card can usually be formatted either as portable storage, which you can move between devices, or as part of the internal storage. For a work device, portable is simpler.

7. Install the Apps and Test Them Properly

Install in this order: your job management or quoting app, cloud storage, email, a PDF reader if drawings are part of your work, and maps. Then test each one on a pretend job rather than assuming it works because it opened. For the job app, create a test customer, fill in a job sheet, take a photo inside it, collect a signature with your finger and send a quote to your own email. For drawings, open the biggest PDF you have and zoom into a detail. For cloud storage, take a photo and watch it appear on your phone or office PC.

If an app you rely on is Windows only, that should already have decided the device; our guide to Android versus Windows has a five minute test. Either way, check the apps on the device before you rely on them. We do not test third party software on our devices, and a vendor's minimum requirements are what to go by.

Two Tuga-specific checks while you are here. On the A6, which has a built-in Zebra 2D barcode scanner, press one of the two side scan keys with a text box open and scan a barcode off a parcel or a box of fittings; the number should appear as typed text. On the scanner versions of the WH6, W8 and W10, do the same with the scan trigger. If you bought a device for scanning, this is the test that proves it. The built-in scanner guide explains the difference between a scan engine and the camera.

Finally, remove or disable the apps you will not use. A work tablet with four screens of icons is slower to use with gloves on, and every app you remove is one that cannot send a notification during a customer visit.

8. Turn On Backup

Backup is separate from cloud sync and people confuse the two. Sync keeps your photos and documents in two places. Backup keeps the device's settings, app list and app data, so that if it is lost or replaced, the next one sets itself up. On Android it is under Settings, then Google, then Backup. On Windows 11 it is in Settings, then Accounts, then Windows backup. Switch both on, then check the job app's own settings, because many trade apps keep job data on their own servers and only need you to be signed in.

Then do the test that nobody does: pick one job sheet or photo and find it on another device. If you can, the backup is real. If you cannot, fix it today rather than the day the tablet goes under a van wheel.

9. Fit the Protection and the Kit

A sealed, drop rated device does not need a case to survive, but a few items make it easier to carry and keep. Fit the Tempered Glass Screen Protector (two in a pack for £14) now, on a clean screen indoors, because a protector fitted on a dusty site will have grit under it for the rest of its life. The A6, A10, W8 and W10 come with a hand strap in the box; for the A8 and WH6 a Hand Strap is £24 and a Belt Holster is £22. A Shoulder Strap is £19 if you want the tablet hanging rather than held, and the Rugged Carry Case is £34 for transport in the van. Everything is on the accessories page.

For charging on the move, the 12V DC Car Charger at £26 fits every device in the range, and the Charging Dock at £49.99 and the WH6 Charging Cradle at £79 give you somewhere to drop the device at the end of the day. If the tablet will live in a vehicle, the Vehicle Mounting Dock is £109, and our guide to mounting a tablet in a van covers where to put it. A Capacitive Stylus at £14.99 is worth having if signatures and drawing mark-ups are part of your day. The Android models are USB-C only, so a USB-C to USB-A OTG Adapter at £8 is the way to plug in a memory stick or a wired keyboard.

10. Register the Warranty and Note the Serial

Every Tuga device has a 12 month warranty whether you register or not, but registering ties the serial number to you, which turns a claim into one email rather than a search for the receipt. The serial is on the box label and in the device's About screen. It takes two minutes on our warranty registration page. While you have the serial in front of you, add it to wherever you keep business records, along with the date and the account it is signed in with. If you are setting up several devices for a team, a list of serials against names is the thing you will want in a year's time; our guide to buying rugged tablets for a small team covers standardising the setup.

The Checklist

  1. Fit the battery if it came separately. Charge.
  2. Join Wi-Fi, fit the SIM, close the seal properly, test mobile data.
  3. Run every system update, restart, set updates to out of hours.
  4. Set a PIN, and the fingerprint sensor where the device has one.
  5. Sign in with a business controlled account. Turn on find my device.
  6. Fit a memory card if you want one. Set the camera to save to it.
  7. Install the job app, cloud storage, email, PDF reader and maps. Test each on a pretend job. Test the scanner if you have one.
  8. Turn on backup and sync. Find one file from another device to prove it.
  9. Fit the screen protector indoors. Fit the strap, holster or mount. Put the car charger in the van.
  10. Register the warranty and record the serial number.

If you are still choosing the device, the four question picker narrows it to one model, and if you are going paperless at the same time, our paperless guide covers the order to set up job sheets, quotes and invoices. Questions about a specific setup, get in touch.
